message.content:
Can you help me draft a power of attorney document tailored to my needs?

Below is a clear, comprehensive, and reproducible example that answers that question by providing guidance and a sample durable power of attorney (POA) document you can adapt. This example contains explanatory paragraphs and a ready-to-edit template.

1) Quick overview — what a power of attorney does and decisions to make
- A power of attorney (POA) is a legal document in which you (the principal) authorize another person (the agent or attorney-in-fact) to act on your behalf.
- Decide the scope: financial matters only, healthcare only, or both. Decide whether powers are broad or limited to specific acts (e.g., handling bank accounts, selling property).
- Choose whether the POA is durable (remains effective if you become incapacitated) or non-durable (ends on incapacity).
- Decide the effective date: immediately upon signing, or only upon a specified event (springing POA).
- Name successor agents in case the primary agent cannot serve.
- Consider specifying limitations, reporting requirements, compensation, and whether the agent must post a bond.
- Check state (or country) law for required language, formalities, witness/notarization rules, and any statutory provisions that should be included.

2) Sample Durable Financial Power of Attorney — template (adapt to your jurisdiction)
Notes before use:
- Replace bracketed placeholders ([...]) with your information.
- Review and modify powers to match your needs.
- Consult a local attorney to ensure the document meets state law and your particular circumstances.
- Sign in the presence of any required witnesses and a notary, if your jurisdiction requires it.

Durable Financial Power of Attorney

I, [Principal’s full name], of [Principal’s address], hereby appoint [Agent’s full name], of [Agent’s address], as my Attorney-in-Fact (Agent) to act for me in any lawful way with respect to my property and financial affairs as described below.

1. Effective Date and Durability
This Power of Attorney is effective immediately upon execution and shall not be affected by my subsequent disability or incapacity. This power of attorney shall continue until my death, unless I revoke it earlier in writing.

2. Grant of General Authority
Subject to any restrictions in this document, I grant my Agent full power and authority to do and perform all acts that I could do with respect to my property and financial affairs, including but not limited to:
- Real property transactions: buy, sell, mortgage, lease, manage, or transfer real estate.
- Banking transactions: open, access, close, and manage bank accounts; endorse checks; make deposits and withdrawals.
- Investment transactions: buy, sell, exchange, and manage stocks, bonds, mutual funds, and other investments.
- Personal and family maintenance: make payments for my daily living expenses, housing, utilities, healthcare not covered by medical powers, education, and support for family members.
- Tax matters: prepare, sign, and file federal, state, and local tax returns; represent me before tax authorities.
- Business operations: operate, buy, sell, or otherwise manage business interests to the same extent I could if personally present.
- Gifts and transfers: make gifts or transfers only as follows: [describe dollar limits, recipients, or state "no gifts allowed" if you wish].

3. Special Instructions and Limitations
[Insert any limitations or special instructions here, for example: “Agent may not sell the family home without my prior written consent” or “Agent may not make gifts exceeding $5,000 per year to any single recipient.”]

4. Successor Agents
If [Agent’s full name] is unable or unwilling to serve, I appoint [Successor Agent’s full name] of [Successor Agent’s address] as successor Agent. If the successor is unavailable, then [Additional Successor(s) ...].

5. Agent’s Duties and Standards
My Agent shall act in my best interests, keep records of transactions, avoid conflicts of interest, and, upon my reasonable request, provide an accounting of actions taken on my behalf.

6. Compensation and Bond
My Agent shall be entitled to reasonable compensation for services rendered unless I expressly provide otherwise. My Agent shall not be required to post bond unless required by law.

7. Revocation
This Power of Attorney may be revoked by me at any time by a written notice delivered to my Agent and any third parties relying on this document.

8. Governing Law
This document shall be governed by the laws of the State of [State] (or specify jurisdiction).

9. Signatures, Acknowledgement, and Witnesses
Executed on this [day] day of [month], [year].

Principal:
______________________________
[Principal’s printed name]

Witnesses (if required by state law):
1. _____________________________  Date: ____________
   [Witness 1 printed name], Address: ___________________

2. _____________________________  Date: ____________
   [Witness 2 printed name], Address: ___________________

Notary Acknowledgement (if required):
State of ________________
County of _______________
On this ____ day of ____________, 20__, personally appeared [Principal’s name], known to me (or proven) to be the person whose name is signed to the foregoing instrument, and acknowledged that he/she executed the same for the purposes therein contained.
______________________________
Notary Public
My commission expires: ______________

3) Example filled-in excerpt (illustrative)
- Principal: Maria J. Alvarez, 123 Oak Lane, Springfield, ST 00000
- Agent: Daniel A. Alvarez, 456 Pine Road, Springfield, ST 00000
- Successor Agent: Priya K. Shah, 789 Maple Ave, Springfield, ST 00000
- Special instruction: “Agent may not make gifts of more than $2,500 in a calendar year to any individual. Agent may not sell the primary residence without written consent from my adult child, Lucia Alvarez, unless a court determines sale is necessary.”

4) Practical steps to finalize
- Review the powers and limitations; tailor language to what you want the agent to be able to do.
- Add any healthcare POA or living will documents if you want medical decision-making authority separated or included.
- Verify witness/notary requirements in your jurisdiction; many states require notarization for a POA to be valid.
- Consider storing the original in a safe place and giving certified copies to your agent, successor agent, and key financial institutions or attorneys.
- Periodically review and update the POA after major life changes (marriage, divorce, childbirth, relocation, changes in assets, or loss of trust in the agent).
